#4088. Grand Theft Auto VI Review - Outrageous Fortune

Many superlatives will be heard in the discussion around Grand Theft Auto VI – biggest world, most activities, best graphics, deepest narrative – but its real triumph is the way all those features and others work in service of a cohesive, believable immersion in a criminal fantasy that is hard to grasp until you’ve played it for yourself.

Rockstar’s latest returns players to a dramatically expanded version of the Vice City seen in a prior game, now largely unrecognizable after real and in-game years have passed. Leonida is a joy to explore, filled with a wealth of activities, both mundane and illicit. The game’s design makes many ordinary tasks as compelling as the illegal ones. Go fishing off the boat, brew coffee to wake up, work out at the gym, scuba dive for long-lost treasure, dust crops, motocross in the mud, go dancing at the club. As you move between those activities, the world feels alive with minor events, from traffic accidents to shady individuals a little too interested in your walk to the ATM. GTAVI delights in life's minutiae, with animations, voice lines, and background characters that keep things fresh even dozens of hours into the story. The level of detail everywhere is astounding and, at times, overwhelming. Getting sidetracked is easy.

The focus on detail carries into the visuals. Lucia’s hair blows in the wind, and she absently pushes it back behind her ear. A drug den is littered with paraphernalia and empty containers. A shifty contact quirks a smile – your only hint that things are about to go south. Sweat glistens on your character’s skin after a hard workout, their breathing and heart rate noticeably heightened. Clouds roll together in the sky, creating realistic weather simulations. The commitment to an authentic simulated world is encompassing, thoughtful, and intentional, a testament to hand-crafted and meticulously painstaking development work, paying off in an absorbing play-space that is hard to step away from.

While the day-to-day simulation is fascinating, it also adds pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward. Not even one of these meticulously choreographed sequences deserves to be spoiled; they run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect.

Ranged combat is punchy and enjoyable; smart use of cover and time-slowing focus makes most battles manageable. On-foot navigation is in a similar boat – simple to pick up and uninterested in needless complexity or challenge; the focus is on choosing smart moments for stealth, knowing when to run and when to fight, and selecting the precise instant for a burst of sudden action. Driving is fast and intense, made more appealing by a huge variety of functionally distinct vehicles to enjoy. If there’s a fault to the core and optional story missions, it’s that many feel a bit on rails regarding where to go and what to do at each step. At the same time, that directed approach keeps the pace relentless, and the action and outcomes thrilling. Over many hours, the game morphs and throws new wrenches into the mix at key junctures, teasing and then playing out criminal experiences from petty theft to group heists to illicit spec ops, and punctuates those distinct vibes with memorable and singular moments.

Like its predecessors, GTAVI simultaneously lampoons and celebrates life in modern America, taking aim at targets like social media, wellness lifestyles, rap and music culture, manosphere content, and dozens more. The caricatures land so well because, in many cases, they’re (sadly) barely over the line of the absurdity we see reflected in real life, and because Rockstar so ably captures individual subcultures, dialects, and situations. Behind it all is a scathing critique of wealth inequality and the inherent unfairness of a system that sets most up to fail. It’s a bitter message delivered in honey-wrapped, exhilarating gameplay, but it shines through.

Of all its significant feats, the relationship between Lucia and Jason elevates the game to new heights, lending this installment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries. This is, without a doubt, video gaming’s most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you’re left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts. The two collectively suffer the slings and arrows of a world that always seems stacked against them; the fortune they amass is not a power grab, but a desperate attempt to cling to each other and come out the other side together, and the player can’t help but cheer them on and dread how fate might stand in the way.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a generational game that stands toe-to-toe with many of the great crime stories and satires across other media. It showcases both the entertainment value of interactive play and the current high-water mark for technical and artistic detail in games. Hunt for and count up all the minor faults or foibles you like, but then note how you just spent another hour lost in this remarkable escape into criminality, wanton violence, egregious sex, and the elusive potential of true love.

Alex Van Aken contributed to this article.

#4087. No Org No Problem beat Stallions Esports 2-1 to reach VCT EMEA Kickoff MENA grand final

No Org No Problem won the opening and deciding maps against Stallions Esports to reach the MENA Qualifier Playoffs grand final. One more series win against Mix My Miks would send them to VCT EMEA Kickoff 2027 in Berlin alongside partner teams including Fnatic.

Against Stallions Esports, the semi-final went the full distance. No Org No Problem took the opening map in 48 minutes. Stallions Esports levelled on the second, winning a 54-minute contest. No Org No Problem then closed out the decider in 43 minutes.

The result came against a ranked opponent. Stallions Esports sat at rank 72 in the Elo power rankings, with a rating of 1628 and a 24-14 record in 38 rated matches. No Org No Problem are unranked. Stallions had also arrived in mixed form, with two 0-2 defeats to VillianArc in VCL MENA: Resilience Pulse Stage Middle East 2026. They beat Spire Esports twice and AXE in the same competition.

No Org No Problem reached the playoffs by winning Middle East Qualifier 1, held from 9 to 11 November, with The Spiders finishing second. Stallions Esports won Middle East Qualifier 2 from 16 to 18 November, ahead of Mayhem. Mix My Miks won North Africa Qualifier 1, a single-elimination event from 9 to 11 November, ahead of BAAM Esports. Each of those qualifiers had 64 teams.

Mix My Miks booked their final place by beating Gamax Esports in the second semi-final. That match also went to three maps. The four-team playoffs are being played online in a single-elimination bracket. The semi-finals were best of three.

Alongside the MENA winner, Europe sends two qualifiers to Berlin and Türkiye sends one. The partner teams already in the field are BBL Esports, Fnatic, FUT Esports, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp, Team Heretics, Team Liquid and Team Vitality. Fnatic were confirmed in October 2026 as staying on as a VCT EMEA partner for 2027.

The tournament will be played in person at the Riot Games Arena in Berlin in early 2027. For the MENA winner, the trip carries direct financial value. Riot’s support for non-partner teams starts at Kickoff, and the sums rise for teams that progress further through the season.

Non-partner teams that qualify for Masters receive US$200,000, and those reaching Champions receive US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. Europe’s route to Kickoff runs in parallel. The Europe Kickoff Qualifier Playoffs begin with a Swiss stage from 25 to 29 November, followed by playoffs from 3 to 5 December.

#4084. Team Cherry Teases New Silksong DLC Info After Months of Silence

Patrick Souza is a writer for DualShockers who has been writing for over 5 years, specializing in JRPGs, roguelikes, and other genres such as MMOs. He previously worked for Prima Games, The Escapist, and The Gamer, and holds a degree in Journalism.

Get ready to return to Pharloom as the previously announced Hollow Knight: Silksong DLC might be closer than you imagined. Team Cherry has just announced a new presentation stream named Cherry Time!, where they’re promising to give us new info on the previously announced expansion for their latest game.

Hollow Knight: Silksong lived up to its hype when it was first released back in 2025, and just like its predecessor, it didn’t take long until a new update was announced. However, in a very Silksong fashion, we barely had any new info on it, aside from its name and a promise to be “coming soon”.

It seems that Team Cherry’s playtesters faced a much tougher Silksong.

This is the first time we’ll be getting an actual update on this expansion, which has only received a single teaser trailer so far. And the Silksong announcement might not be the only thing we’ll be seeing here.

Throughout its social media accounts, Team Cherry has announced their Cherry Time! Livestream, a new presentation they haven’t done before. You can watch it live on November 27, 7 AM PT on their official YouTube channel.

Team Cherry is promising “a bunch of exciting announcements” aside from the already expected info on Sea of Sorrow, the Silksong DLC. This could be either new updates for the game, unrelated to the DLC, or even new titles from one of the world’s most secluded dev teams.

Aside from the initial trailer released back in 2025, the team has been radio silent about its development. This might actually be a great sign, as you’ll know if you’ve followed anything about Silksong’s development cycle in the past years.

The game was originally conceived as an expansion for the original Hollow Knight, where you could play as the supporting character Hornet. However, the project became too big for its own good, eventually turning into a whole new game in just a few years.

This could be either new updates for the game, unrelated to the DLC, or even new titles from one of the world’s most secluded dev teams.

However, Team Cherry was adamant about never feeding us any new info, leading fans to think the game was quietly canceled or that it was all a hoax from the start. You’ll certainly remember those frenzied fans typing “SKONG??!!” on every single indie game announcement stream (or any stream, really). Things got out of control at a time.

Imagine the shock when we discovered Team Cherry was just too busy adding new things to the game over the years and had adopted a chronically offline posture. We only got actual info less than a month before the game actually came out. We might be seeing history repeating itself here, but I wouldn’t count on it just yet.

While we were promised that the waiting wouldn’t be as daunting as it was for the base game (which took 8 years to release after the first title), it seems like Sea of Sorrow might be going through the same development hell cycle.

For all we know, Team Cherry might be taking their time cooking another huge meal for us once again. It certainly won’t take 8 more years again, but we might not be visiting this new ocean of content this year just yet.

The original Hollow Knight had a total of four free updates, which added tons of content such as new endings, more quests, new bosses, and many boss gauntlets to prove yourself as a real God in Hallownest. Fans have huge expectations for Silksong to get the same treatment, especially when it comes to the latter.

We’ll know more about the current state of this expansion in just a few more days. We got a release date for Silksong similarly, coming almost out of nowhere, so it might be the time. But as we’ve seen lately, devs have been taking extra time to refine their final game, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see that happen here, too.

#4082. QoR sweep Maryville to reach VCT Americas Kickoff North America playoffs after opening loss

QoR's 2-0 win over Maryville University completed a recovery from an opening defeat at the VCT Americas Kickoff North America qualifiers. A Kickoff place and a Red Bull Home Ground spot both stay within QoR's reach as a result.

The line-up of ExpMoe, calamity, vanitas, yearn and dynamic was one of eight teams Riot Games invited directly to the North America Qualifier Playoffs. Cloud9, ENVY and two Shopify Rebellion line-ups were also on that list.

Before facing Maryville, QoR edged Shopify Rebellion Gold 2-1 in round two. In the Swiss stage, two wins sent a team through and two losses knocked it out. QoR sit 99th in the Elo power rankings, with a rating of 1590 and a 37-34 record across 71 rated matches.

Maryville came through the second open qualifier, held from 12 to 15 November, which drew 512 teams. They finished in the top two of that bracket. They then opened this event by sweeping Shopify Rebellion Gold.

A 0-2 loss to Cloud9 followed, and defeat by QoR left them with two losses. In the other round-three matches, Oafs beat SaD Esports, counterfeit beat FlyQuest and Wildcard beat Winthrop, each without dropping a map. The Elo table places Maryville 161st, with a rating of 1521 and a 6-7 record in 13 rated matches.

The playoffs are an eight-team double-elimination bracket. The winner takes North America’s direct place at the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in São Paulo. The runner-up goes to the Americas Last Chance Qualifier, also in São Paulo, on 17 and 18 December. That event is the last route into Kickoff. Eight partner teams are invited to Kickoff, and four places go to non-partner teams.

Riot runs the North America qualifiers with Red Bull. They also serve as the North America qualifiers for Red Bull Home Ground. The Los Angeles event runs from 10 to 13 December. Ten teams will play for a total prize pool of $100,000 USD. Eight are invited from around the world, and two earn their places through regional qualifiers. Riot will also reveal the 2027 Kickoff draws live on stage there.

Fnatic are EMEA’s invited team. The organisation is rebuilding its roster after parting with several players, including long-serving captain Jake ‘Boaster’ Howlett, Red Bull said.

The North America playoff bracket opens on 1 December.

#4081. Monster Hunter Rise now available worldwide for mobile on Netflix Games

Early in October, we got probably our most exciting addition to the Netflix Games lineup in a while, as Monster Hunter Rise made a surprise drop in select regions. Now, those of you who've been waiting with bated breath will be excited to learn that Monster Hunter Rise is now out fully on Netflix Games for all eligible regions!

If I were a business guy, I'd probably wonder whether this might split the audience. And in truth, although I'm glad you'll have more options as a Monster Hunter fan, it does raise the question whether the split in attention will affect MHO negatively.

Still, that's a question for the philosophers- for now, it just means that if you want to experience Monster Hunter on mobile, you're more spoilt for choice than ever! And if MHO and Rise are any indication, the new standard has already been set for the monster-slaying franchise.

Why not try something a little more heartfelt and check out my review of Vampire Therapist to find out why I think this therapy-themed visual novel is well worth playing for vampire fans and narrative lovers alike!

#4080. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

Honkai: Star Rail's next major update introduces a whole new planet to the RPG, and way more besides.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

#4079. We Got These 102 Things Before GTA VI

Grand Theft Auto VI is here. Let’s pat ourselves on the back; we made it. While it's a day of jubilation for many, it’s also a day of mourning as we’re losing an important piece of our cultural fabric: the “We got ________ before GTA VI” meme.

#4078. Take-Two's GTA 6 PC Port Crackdown Has Already Taken Down Over 3,000 Repositories

Grand Theft Auto 6 is still a console exclusive, but some fans have already been trying to get it running on PC. Take-Two Interactive has filed a copyright complaint against Leonida, an unofficial port based on the Xbox Series version of the game. It's not just the original project that's been affected: GitHub has taken action against a whopping 3,007 repositories in response to the complaint.

According to a new rumor, Rockstar Games could release the GTA 6 PC port just a few months after the highly anticipated console launch.

Leonida was named after the fictional state in which GTA 6 takes place, and it was one of several attempts to get the console version running on a computer. Unlike some of the fan-made PC ports we've seen for older console games, though, this one was being developed using a build of a game that had only just come out.

In a DMCA notice published on GitHub on November 24, Take-Two's intellectual property enforcement team alleges that Leonida infringes upon the company's copyright and violates Rockstar's terms of service. The notice says an Xbox Series build of GTA 6 was leaked on November 20, with the Leonida repository appearing a day later.

The developers had asked users to supply their own game files, but Take-Two argues that the project was designed specifically to make use of the leaked build. The company requested that GitHub take down Leonida and its forks, arguing that the alleged infringement couldn't be addressed without disabling the repositories altogether.

GitHub says it acted on the entire network of 3,007 repositories. That number includes forks, which are essentially copies of a repository that other GitHub users can work on independently. That doesn't mean there were 3,007 different GTA 6 PC ports in development, though.

An Xbox Series build of GTA 6 was leaked on November 20, with the Leonida repository appearing a day later.

According to PC Gamer, the team appeared to have reached the game's splash screen during a livestream before it crashed. The project's lead developer, NotRexed, subsequently announced their departure, citing the loss of the Discord server as well as the pressure of managing the community alongside school and sports.

Take-Two's takedown hasn't put an end to Leonida, either. According to the same report, others have already tried to pick up where the original developer left off.

It's a familiar situation for those of us who primarily play on PC. GTA 4 came to PC several months after its console debut, while we had to wait more than a year and a half after GTA 5's original launch for its PC version. Even Red Dead Redemption 2 took roughly a year to make its way over.

The difference this time is that a report has suggested GTA 6 could arrive on PC in the first quarter of 2027. If that turns out to be true, the wait would be much shorter than it was for Rockstar's last two major releases. There hasn't been an official announcement confirming that release window, however.

Getting GTA 6 to boot on a PC and getting it to run well enough to play through the entire game are two very different things. Just look at how badly Rockstar handled GTA 4's PC port. Even hardware that far exceeded the game's original system requirements struggled to run it smoothly, and Rockstar never bothered to properly fix it.

Modders have spent years ironing out its performance issues and bugs, and while that's still an ongoing process, I'd argue 2026 has been the best year yet to play GTA 4 on PC. Even if one of these unofficial efforts eventually makes it past the splash screen, there's no telling how well the game will run on a typical gaming PC or whether it'll have major bugs throughout the story.

Hopefully, Rockstar won't keep us in the dark for too long regarding the official PC version. Even an approximate release window would be welcome at this point, especially for anyone holding off on buying a console just to play GTA 6.

#4077. GodLike Esports sweep Trigger Point Esports to stay unbeaten in South Asia Kickoff qualifier

GodLike Esports beat Trigger Point Esports 2-0 in the upper bracket of the VCT Pacific Kickoff South Asia qualifier. Only two South Asian sides will reach the Last Chance Qualifier, where a single place at Kickoff in Bangkok is on offer.

GodLike Esports opened their VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 playoff campaign with a 2-0 win over Trigger Point Esports on Monday 23 November 2026. GodLike took both maps of the best-of-three upper bracket quarter-final. Trigger Point Esports now drop into the lower bracket of the double-elimination format.

The playoffs are being held online by Riot Games and JioBLAST. Series in the bracket are played as best-of-three or best-of-five.

GodLike arrived in form. They reached the playoffs with an unbeaten 4-0 record in the open qualifier, VLR.gg reported. They shared joint first to fourth place in that event, which ran from 17 to 20 November. Trigger Point finished in the group placed fifth to eighth.

GodLike fielded Karam1L, Paradox and RvK from India, alongside sayoo from Indonesia and azyshaha from the Philippines. Sabyasachi ‘Antidote’ Bose is listed as head coach, with Samar as substitute. Trigger Point’s listed players are SangraM, WEELJACK and RaJ.

South Asian teams cannot qualify directly for Kickoff. The top two from the playoffs join the Oceania playoff winner and the Southeast Asia playoff runner-up in a four-team Last Chance Qualifier. Only its winner goes through to Kickoff in Bangkok, according to Dot Esports.

The stakes are high. Twelve teams will play at Kickoff, and the top three will qualify for Masters 1. The route stays narrow later in the season too. South Asia has no direct place at the Cups, with Cup 1 in Manila and Cup 2 in Tokyo. It sends two teams to an eight-team Pacific LCQ, and the winner takes the last Cup place.

The qualifier also has a new organiser. Riot picked JioBLAST to run the South Asia qualifiers instead of NODWIN Gaming, the previous organiser. Riot has not said why it made the change.

The UK interest lies with SIGN Esports. They beat Zexar Esports 2-0 in another upper bracket quarter-final. Russel ‘Russ’ Mendes joined SIGN Esports on 16 November 2026. He is the only player from the UK in the eight-team playoff field.

Russ was born in 1998 and is of Indian descent. He won the VALORANT Challengers 2025 South Asia Grand Final with Velocity Gaming on 13 July 2025, when they beat S8UL 3-1.

GodLike Esports and SIGN Esports both remain in the upper bracket, one defeat away from the lower bracket. Trigger Point Esports and Zexar Esports must win from the lower bracket to stay in contention for a top-two finish. The playoffs run until 29 November 2026.
